mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that lowers discount rates for equities, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises by more than 0.3 percentage points over a 3-month period, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce corporate earnings expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances, or Rank IC over 2-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts and retail sales indicate robust consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS rise, or interaction term regression coefficient is negative with p>0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In a stagflationary supply shock regime (characterized by declining industrial production and rising inflation), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns due to reduced corporate profit margins and increased risk aversion over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods classified as stagflationary supply shock, or Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A positive quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1) indicates robust economic expansion that supports corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods with positive GDPC1 growth, or Rank IC over 2-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0%, it signals persistent inflation that triggers aggressive monetary tightening expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 3.0% YoY, or Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in payroll employment and declines in the unemployment rate indicate a tightening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls, or interaction term regression coefficient is negative with p>0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In a high interest rate environment (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), further increases in the federal funds rate signal aggressive monetary tightening that reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and FEDFUNDS rises, or Rank IC over 2-year windows is below 0.03.
